answer.text: Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly as the command module pilot on Apollo 13. The swap was made because Mattingly had no rubella (German measles) immunity: blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed he was the only one of the five prime and backup crew members without antibodies. Backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke had caught German measles and exposed the crews, and flight surgeon Charles Berry worried Mattingly could fall ill alone in the command module in lunar orbit. The decision was made at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (sources: [apollo-13-measles-article], [rubella-crew-swap], [ken-mattingly], [apollo-13]).

answer.text: Jack Swigert replaced Ken Mattingly on Apollo 13 as command module pilot. The reason was rubella (German measles) exposure: blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Mattingly had no rubella immunity, and flight surgeon Charles Berry worried he could fall ill alone in the command module in lunar orbit after backup lunar module pilot Charlie Duke caught German measles and exposed the crews. The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced on 1970-04-10. Swigert was immune to rubella, which made him eligible to fly. (Sources: apollo-13-measles-article, rubella-crew-swap, jack-swigert)

answer.text: The command module pilot was changed because of a rubella (German measles) exposure. Charlie Duke, the backup lunar module pilot, caught German measles, and blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. Flight surgeon Charles Berry worried Mattingly could fall ill alone in the command module in lunar orbit, so a KSC management meeting decided on the swap, announced on 1970-04-10, replacing Mattingly with Jack Swigert (who was immune). Mattingly was reassigned to Apollo 16. (Sources: rubella-crew-swap; apollo-13 fact lines citing the NASA history Apollo 13 measles article.)
